findings.title: Data quality improvement through deduplication
findings.statement: Removing 12 duplicate rows improved the overall data quality score from 97.1 to 100.0 out of 100.
findings.recommendation: Maintain the current deduplication process to ensure data integrity in future ingestion cycles.

findings.title: Significant temperature skewness
findings.statement: The temperature distribution remains heavily skewed at -7.77, indicating a non-normal distribution of readings.
findings.recommendation: Consider using non-parametric statistical methods or robust scaling when analyzing temperature trends.

findings.title: Humidity readings show minimal outliers
findings.statement: Humidity data is relatively stable with only 4 IQR outliers, accounting for 0.67% of the cleaned records.
findings.recommendation: Continue monitoring humidity, as current data quality appears high for this metric.

findings.title: Lack of strong linear associations
findings.statement: There are no significant linear correlations between variables, and sensor_id has 0.5 unique pct threshold references in the column profile context.
findings.recommendation: Explore non-linear modeling techniques if you suspect a relationship exists between these variables.

narrative.headline: Cleaned sensor readings dataset achieves a perfect 100.0 out of 100 quality score after deduplication.
narrative.executive_summary: The sensor_readings.csv dataset was successfully cleaned, improving the data quality score from 97.1 to 100.0 out of 100 by removing 12 duplicate rows down to 600 records. Temperature readings exhibit heavy skewness at -7.77, while humidity data remains stable with only 4 IQR outliers accounting for 0.67 percent of the cleaned records. Furthermore, the analysis reveals no significant linear correlations between variables, and sensor_id has 0.5 unique pct threshold references in the column profile context.
next_steps: Address the heavily skewed temperature distribution at -7.77 using non-normal modeling techniques.
Investigate the 4 IQR outliers in humidity data representing 0.67 percent of records.
Account for the lack of strong linear associations between variables in future predictive modeling.
Utilize the cleaned 600 records for monitoring room temperature and humidity.
